text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The World Food program (WFP) delivers one metric ton of protein biscuits to the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia in support of its humanitarian activities, the WFP says.
- Three companies in central town of Zenica say they are being deprived of promised World Bank credits and that local authorities have allegedly shifted the credits elsewhere, paper reports.
- Moslem-Croat federation premier Edhem Bicakcic says that federation will take over problem of gas heating and warns that government officials can retain their posts only if they work effectively.
- Metropolitan Nikolaj, top Ortodox Christian leader in Bosnia sends New Year's greetings to the chairman of Bosnian collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic and to all Bosnia's national communities.

- Croatian state television conducts media war over the last month by interfering with state television signal, Bosnian state television general menager Amila Omersoftic says. Such interference did not occur during the war.
- International Police Task Force (IPTF) and Bosnian Croat police prevent further expulsions of Moslems from the Croat controlled part of the divided Bosnian town of Mostar.
